text:
sara_ml: quick sync — onboarding checklist for `saber-v1` weights + tokenizer quirks. I pushed weights to gs://redwood-weights/onboard/saber-v1/ but CI flagged missing metadata. Anyone able to confirm exact path and checksum?

omar_infra: I see a `saber-v1` folder at gs://redwood-weights/onboard/saber-v1/2024-03-10/weights.tar.gz sha256: 3b9f...ef12. Did CI want a manifest.json next to it?

sara_ml: yep CI expects manifest.json with model_size + tokenizer_name + sha256. I added a minimal one but want to validate tokenizer name — model was trained with `sentencepiece_saber` but tokenizer in weights is `saber-sp`. Could that mismatch break serving?

jess_prod: mismatch will cause our onboarding validator to try to load nonexistent tokenizer config. In practice runtime falls back but that can change token IDs (bad). We should standardize name in manifest to the package name we publish, i.e. `saber-sp`.

kai: quick tokenizer quirk: when I encoded chat templates the dataset team used a custom sentinel token `<|assistant|>` but our current chatfmt expects `<|assistant|>\n` (note trailing newline). That produced an extra token at end sometimes — seen as off-by-one in KV cache.

sara_ml: ugh — do we have a recommended remediation? strip trailing newline in templates or add a special mapping in tokenizer config?

omar_infra: option A: canonicalize the template generator to never append the sentinel newline. Option B: add `sentinel_aliases` to tokenizer.json so both map to same special id. I prefer A for long-term.

jess_prod: for immediate unblock, add `sentinel_aliases: ["<|assistant|>\n"]` to tokenizer.json and update manifest. Also add test case: `encode("...<|assistant|>\n") == encode("...<|assistant|>")`.

kai: noted. Also saw BOS/EOS behavior: `tokenizer.encode("\nHello")` returns an extra BOS token for some versions of sentencepiece wrapper. That shifts positions for prefix caching. We should add a small shim in our serving loader that normalizes leading/trailing BOS/EOS if `preserve_bos_eos` not set in manifest.

sara_ml: good call. I'll update manifest schema: add `normalize_bos_eos: true|false` default true. If true loader will strip house-added BOS/EOS from examples before caching.

deploy-bot: CI check started for PR #4123 — manifest schema validation + weights checksum.

omar_infra: FYI weights path is duplicated under s3 as well: s3://redwood-archive/onboard/saber-v1/weights.tar.gz same sha256. We can keep both but manifest should list primary_uri array.

jess_prod: can someone post the exact manifest snippet we'll land on? small example please.

sara_ml: snippet I'm going to push to PR:
```
{
 "model_name": "saber-v1",
 "primary_uris": ["gs://redwood-weights/onboard/saber-v1/2024-03-10/weights.tar.gz"],
 "sha256": "3b9f...ef12",
 "tokenizer_name": "saber-sp",
 "tokenizer_config": {"sentinel_aliases": ["<|assistant|>\n"], "normalize_bos_eos": true}
}
```

kai: looks good. Add `tokenizer_version` too so we can detect behavior drift.

sara_ml: will add `tokenizer_version: "sp-0.9.1"`. Also adding a quick unit to onboarding tests: run `python -c "from tokenizers import load; print(load(...).encode('<|assistant|>\n')==load(...).encode('<|assistant|>'))"` as CI smoke.

omar_infra: after PR lands I'll trigger a dedicated rollout to a canary pool with `--normalize-bos-eos` off to validate no regressions. plan: 24h canary, compare token counts and latency.

jess_prod: if canary shows stable, we promote. Also add a console alert for any route using saber-v1 that has tokenization mismatch >2% in a day.

sara_ml: thanks everyone. I'll open PR in ~30m and ping for quick reviews. :thumbsup:

kai: ping me on the PR for a quick tokenization unit review.

omar_infra: pinged in #eng-infra about storage lifecycle policy for onboarded buckets — don't let these weights expire.

jess_prod: noted. adding retention override to manifest as `retention_days: 3650` so infra doesn't GC.

sara_ml: perfect. closing this thread once PR merged. back to async work — thanks!
